feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. Evidence: iterations 0 to 2 (60 development trials each) all ended off track with progress of 0.10 to 0.15, one line-loss event per run, and max_error of about 0.062 m, just above the 0.06 m limit. Gain changes (iteration 1, kp 2.0 to 2.5 and ki 0.05 to 0.3) and the sensor span change to x = ±0.04 with base_speed 1.6 to 1.3 (iteration 2) moved progress only slightly. Steering oscillation stayed low, so the robot is not weaving. This candidate changes only base_speed (1.3 to 1.0), with geometry, gains, sensor weights and line_loss unchanged. That isolates speed, the one lever not yet tested alone. It is valid and not obviously broken. It is a diagnostic step that the race can answer, so reading numbers alone will not settle it. Lower speed will hurt completion_time, but the current scores come almost entirely from progress, so this is an acceptable cost for finding the failure cause. Read the next telemetry this way. (1) If progress rises clearly above 0.15 on the oval and s-bend, speed was the cause. Then find a speed between 1.0 and 1.3 that keeps the line and gives more progress, and only then raise speed toward completion. (2) If progress stays near 0.11 to 0.15 even at 1.0, speed is not the cause. Next suspects are the line-loss recovery and turn authority. The line-loss recovery is the more likely target, since the robot leaves the line after one loss and last_direction does not bring it back.
requested_changes: Keep the current geometry and gains and read progress, line_loss_events and max_error per track. If progress rises clearly above 0.15 on the oval and s-bend, keep base_speed near 1.0 to 1.2 and then raise it in small steps to find the fastest speed that still holds the line.

If progress stays near 0.11 to 0.15 at base_speed 1.0, change only controller.line_loss from last_direction to search_right or search_left, chosen by which side max_error grows on. Iteration 0 to 2 all show one loss per run that never recovers, so the recovery mode is the next suspect.

If line loss still occurs with the same recovery mode, lower kp from 2.5 toward 2.0 and check whether the max_error and line-loss point move. This tests whether turn authority at the bend entry causes the loss, which is only worth trying after the recovery mode has been tested alone.
